steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Unplug dishwasher or disconnect power.

steps.title: Continue procedure
steps.body: Service mode entered. Continue with component checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: After service mode entry, proceed with OEM component test steps.

steps.title: Access drain pump
steps.body: Lay dishwasher on back after removing drip pan/float switch. Unplug CON2 from control board.
steps.sourceExcerpt: If the resistance is between 25-35 ohms, the drain pump and harness are good.

steps.title: Drain pump winding resistance
steps.body: Measure across CON2 pin 1 (drain pump) and CON1 pin 1 (neutral). Expect 25–35 Ω.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure across CON2 pin 1 (drain pump) and CON1 pin 1 (neutral). Expect 25–35 Ω.

steps.title: Check valve and impeller
steps.body: Verify check valve flapper moves freely and impeller is not fractured.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Verify check valve flapper moves freely and impeller is not fractured.

steps.title: Replace drain pump
steps.body: Replace drain pump assembly; verify hose and clamp.

steps.title: Drain pump verified
steps.body: Pump ohms in spec and check valve OK.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Unplug dishwasher or disconnect power.

steps.title: E3 behavior
steps.body: E3 displays when water temperature does not reach the correct value within 90 minutes. Quick and Glass indicators flash (non-SSD).
steps.sourceExcerpt: WHEN THE TEMPERATURE DOESN'T REACH THE CORRECT VALUE AFTER 90 MINUTES, E3 WILL BE DISPLAYED.

steps.title: Continue procedure
steps.body: Service mode entered. Continue with component checks below.
steps.sourceExcerpt: After service mode entry, proceed with OEM component test steps.

steps.title: Access heating element
steps.body: Lay unit on back; remove drip pan. Disconnect P02 and CON1 from control board. Access PO1/PO2 heater terminals.
steps.sourceExcerpt: If the resistance is approximately 14 ohms, go to step 7.

steps.title: Heater element resistance
steps.body: Measure between PO1/PO2 and CON1-1 (neutral). Expect approximately 14 Ω.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure between PO1/PO2 and CON1-1 (neutral). Expect approximately 14 Ω.

steps.title: Thermistor follow-up
steps.body: If E3 persists with good heater ohms, run tub thermistor test (w11187658-tub-thermistor) and verify heater relay output.
steps.sourceExcerpt: If E3 persists with good heater ohms, run tub thermistor test (w11187658-tub-thermistor) and verify heater relay output.

steps.title: Replace heater
steps.body: Replace heating element; verify harness continuity.

steps.title: Heater verified
steps.body: Heater ~14 Ω — verify thermistor and control if E3 remains.

procedures.title: E1 — Water inlet failure (4 min fill)

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Unplug dishwasher or disconnect power.

steps.title: E1 behavior
steps.body: E1 displays when the flow meter cannot detect a correct fill after 4 minutes during the inlet step. Quick indicator flashes (SSD) or E1 on seven-segment display.
steps.sourceExcerpt: IF THE FLOW METER CAN'T DETECT A CORRECT FILL AFTER 4 MINUTES, E1 WILL BE DISPLAYED.

steps.title: Water supply and installation
steps.body: Verify supply valve on, 20–100 psi pressure, inlet screen clean, drain hose not siphoning, and dishwasher level.
steps.sourceExcerpt: 1. CHECK THE WATER SUPPLY.

steps.title: Fill circuit inspection
steps.body: Power off. Access kick panel and control board cover. Inspect CN5 inlet harness, CN4 flow meter, pressure switch hose to sump, and drain path. Run fill-valve ohms (w11187658-fill-valve) and drain pump test if needed.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Power off. Access kick panel and control board cover. Inspect CN5 inlet harness, CN4 flow meter, pressure switch hose to sump, and drain path. Run fill-valve ohms (w11187658-fill-valve) and drain pump test if needed.

steps.title: Pressure switch hose
steps.body: Pressure switch hose runs from switch on base bracket to sump. Hose kinked, disconnected, blocked, or leaking?
steps.sourceExcerpt: 5. CHECK THE PRESSURE SWITCH.

steps.title: Flow meter at CN4
steps.body: Inspect CN4 flow meter / thermistor / overflow harness for damage or poor connection at control board.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect CN4 flow meter / thermistor / overflow harness for damage or poor connection at control board.

steps.title: Correct supply issue
steps.body: Restore water supply, correct installation, and retest fill.

steps.title: Repair pressure switch path
steps.body: Repair or replace pressure switch hose; verify switch seated on base bracket.

steps.title: Fill path verified
steps.body: Supply, inlet valve, flow meter, pressure switch, and drain prerequisites checked — retest for E1.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Unplug dishwasher or disconnect power.

steps.title: E4 behavior
steps.body: E4 displays when water flows into the base pan and activates the overflow switch. Light indicator flashes.
steps.sourceExcerpt: IF WATER FLOWS INTO THE BASE AND ACTIVATES THE OVERFLOW SWITCH, THE DISHWASHER WILL DISPLAY E4.

steps.title: Detergent, level, and leak source
steps.body: Check detergent type/amount, appliance level, and visible leak at door gasket, sump, or hoses.
steps.sourceExcerpt: 1. CHECK THE USE OF THE DETERGENT.

steps.title: CN4 overflow switch
steps.body: Inspect CN4 overflow switch harness. Float down: CN4-2 to CN4-3 should read ≤3 Ω. Float up: open circuit.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect CN4 overflow switch harness. Float down: CN4-2 to CN4-3 should read ≤3 Ω. Float up: open circuit.

steps.title: Drain pan and pump
steps.body: Remove standing water from base. Does drain pump run and remove water when commanded in service mode?
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove standing water from base. Does drain pump run and remove water when commanded in service mode?

steps.title: Locate leak
steps.body: With pan dry, run a short fill cycle and inspect sump, door seal, and hose clamps for leak source.
steps.sourceExcerpt: With pan dry, run a short fill cycle and inspect sump, door seal, and hose clamps for leak source.

steps.title: Drain pump bench test
steps.body: Run w11187658-drain-pump for 25–35 Ω winding check and check valve.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Run w11187658-drain-pump for 25–35 Ω winding check and check valve.

steps.title: Correct installation
steps.body: Reduce detergent, level unit, or repair identified leak source.

steps.title: Service drain path
steps.body: Replace drain pump or clear obstruction; dry base pan before retest.

steps.title: Overflow path checked
steps.body: Pan dry, flood switch reset, drain verified — retest for E4.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the dishwasher or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Unplug dishwasher or disconnect power.

steps.title: E6 / E7 behavior
steps.body: E6 = NTC open circuit (Light + Glass flash). E7 = NTC short (Light + Glass + Quick flash). Both affect E3 heat path.
steps.sourceExcerpt: TEMPERATURE SENSOR OPEN CIRCUIT, E6 WILL BE DISPLAYED.

steps.title: Access tub thermistor
steps.body: Lay dishwasher on back; remove drip pan. Thermistor on back of sump — unplug CN4 before ohms.

steps.title: Tub thermistor resistance
steps.body: Measure between CN4-2 (GND) and CN4-7 (RE) at room temperature (~77°F). Expect 10 kΩ.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure between CN4-2 (GND) and CN4-7 (RE) at room temperature (~77°F). Expect 10 kΩ.

steps.title: Harness check
steps.body: Inspect thermistor harness between CN4 and sump. Repair opens before replacing control board.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Inspect thermistor harness between CN4 and sump. Repair opens before replacing control board.

steps.title: Replace thermistor
steps.body: Replace tub thermistor assembly.

steps.title: Thermistor verified
steps.body: NTC in spec — if E6/E7/E3 persist, suspect control board.
